mortonAnnouncement: Coordinates X {x}, Y {y}, Z {z}. Morton key {key}. Position {rank} of 16 in this slice.
mortonPlain: Changing a coordinate interleaves three axes into a sort key. Below, that selected point is sorted with 15 other points in the same slice. Key order is not Euclidean-distance order.
mortonBitsLabel: Interleaved bits · low bits on the right
mortonNumerics: The browser's X, Y, and Z inputs are integer grid cells from 0 to 2^{bits}−1 per axis. The {totalBits}-bit key can exceed JavaScript Number's safe integer range, so this demo uses BigInt. The research Metal path first quantizes real coordinates using an origin and cell size.
formulaEquationAria: Morton key M is the sum from i equals 0 through {last} of x sub i times 2 to the 3 i, y sub i times 2 to the 3 i plus 1, and z sub i times 2 to the 3 i plus 2.
formulaBitRuleAria: Extract bit {index} of each axis by shifting its integer coordinate right by {index} and taking bitwise AND with one.
formulaLaneAria: Move bit {index} of each axis into positions 3 i, 3 i plus 1, and 3 i plus 2.
formulaGroupAria: The three bits form binary {bits}, and this group contributes {value} to the Morton key.
formulaComplete: The three terms at this bit position contribute one part of the key. The full key sums terms from every bit position.
formulaGroup: Selected three bits in the Morton key
formulaNote: Low bits start on the right. At each i, xᵢ, yᵢ, and zᵢ occupy positions 3i, 3i+1, and 3i+2. The three bits below read zᵢ yᵢ xᵢ from high to low.
formulaExact: All positions and the decimal value use exact BigInt arithmetic.
stripHint: Drag horizontally or swipe through the samples. Select a point to load its coordinates.
operatorStageGroup: Squared distance, FPS, kNN, Ball Query, and gradient equations
operatorDistanceNote: Square the coordinate difference on each of three axes and add them. Feature-space kNN extends the sum through D−1.
operatorDistanceAria: s sub b i j equals the sum from d equals zero to two of q sub b i d minus x sub b j d, squared.
operatorFpsNote: Keep each point's minimum squared distance to the selected centers, then choose the point with the largest minimum. The smaller input index wins an exact tie.
operatorFpsAria: m sub j at step t is the minimum squared distance to any selected center. The next center has the maximum m, breaking ties by the smallest input index.
operatorKnnNote: Sort by the pair (squared distance, input index) to select the kth point. Return its Euclidean distance by taking the square root.
operatorKnnAria: pi is the permutation sorted by squared distance then input index. I is the kth index in that permutation; D is the square root of the selected squared distance.
operatorBallNote: Round r to float32 before squaring. Return the first K points in input order whose s < R₂, padding with (−1, 0). At the boundary, Metal FMA and the tiny-radius normalized path can differ in bits from this real-valued expression.
operatorBallAria: R squared is the float32-rounded product of two float32-rounded radius values. Gather points whose squared distance is strictly below R squared, keep the first K in input order, and pad with index minus one and distance zero.
operatorGradientNote: For fixed selected indices, ∂s/∂q=2(q−x) and ∂s/∂x=2(x−q). Multiply by G and sum only valid I≥0. The radius and discrete neighbor choice have no gradient.
operatorGradientAria: The query gradient sums two times G times q minus x over valid selected neighbors. The reference gradient sums two times G times x minus q over queries selecting that reference. Padding indices are ignored.
pruningDeck: Move the circle. The browser tests AABB bounds and counts rejected subtree roots.
pruningCanvasHelp: Move the pointer or use arrow keys on the canvas to move the query. Adjust the radius with the slider. A circle in coordinate units appears elliptical on this wide canvas.
pruningPlain: Only branches whose AABB minimum squared distance exceeds r² are skipped. Equality is traversed; an individual point is a neighbor only when d² < r². The browser computes these values for the current query.
aabbRuleLabel: Lower-bound test for the highlighted AABB
decisionPruned: AABB #{node} has a squared distance lower bound beyond the squared radius, so its subtree was skipped.
decisionVisited: AABB #{node} has a squared distance lower bound at or below the squared radius, so its contents were examined.
decisionChecks: Point distance checks {checked}/{total} · not an execution-time measurement.
pruningAnnouncement: Visited {visited} nodes, rejected {pruned} AABB roots, checked {distances} point distances, found {hits} points
pruningModelNote: This is a browser-computed 2D, single-query model. It Morton-sorts points, bisects balanced {brick}-point bricks, bounds actual coordinates, and collects all radius hits without a K limit. 'Pruned AABB roots' counts each rejected subtree root once, not all descendants. The unreleased research Metal path uses a two-level balanced BVH of {sourceBrick}-point bricks in 3D and returns the first K hits in original input order. These counters are not GPU performance metrics.

routingRule: kNN selects BVH automatically only on {hardware} with Safe Math, N={n}, K={k}, Q={qMin}–{qMax}, and sampled cell occupancy below {density}. Other inputs and all Ball Query Auto calls use full scan. Forced BVH also requires PYTORCH_MPS_FAST_MATH=0 before the process starts, and supports one MPS float32 cloud, N≤{maxN}, K≤{maxK}, within a bounded coordinate domain.
